Focused regression cases for source-page triage

Run `python3 testdata/triage/source-page-review/check.py` from the repository.
The runner accepts an optional Cleave binary path.

The fixtures distinguish CoinHive construction, an expiring opt-out policy,
and an actual start directly gated by that policy. An explicit button handler,
a dormant configuration, a zero/unspecified timeout, a commented HTML block,
and an unrelated constructor are near misses. The two objective rules are
suspicious: the snippet cannot establish consent obtained elsewhere. A full
page can still be malicious when review establishes undisclosed automatic mining.

FSO fixtures distinguish default read, explicit read, overwrite, and append
when the pathname contains a nested function call. A comma inside a pathname
helper must not be treated as the outer OpenTextFile mode argument. The write
umbrella now references the canonical create/overwrite/append atoms rather
than duplicating their regexes; Cleave filters this pure-OR umbrella from
reports, so fixtures assert the concrete operation atoms.

Other controls cover JDBC table backups, ordinary textareas, password and
website controls, Pinterest endpoint references, and an IOCP implementation
reference. Database rows written to a local backup are not HTTP output or an
Oracle-specific behavior. Request access plus a file stream does not prove a
webshell; the unsupported JSP co-occurrence conviction was removed while its
command-shell consumer retains the same required evidence, written directly.

`cases.json` records exact ID relocations. Matchers and effective type/platform
scope are preserved for these moves. The FSO mode fixes, splitting the write
umbrella, removal of the unsupported JSP conviction, narrowing the ASP
allowlist reference, and new request/JDBC/mining coverage are intentional
coverage changes. The moved Boost IOCP reference no longer belongs to the
cryptojacking runtime selector; a generic event-loop marker is not mining.
No new taxonomy leaves or directory budgets are introduced.
